titleEn: The Tibetan Book of the Dead — Karma Heruka on day twelve, and the wrathful goddesses: the Gaurīs, the Phra men, the gatekeepers and the first Īśvarīs
part: 11 · Karma Heruka on day twelve, and the wrathful goddesses: the Gaurīs, the Phra men, the gatekeepers and the first Īśvarīs
draftNote: Read from one blockprint at the resolution of an online scan; doubtful places are marked in the notes, and the text has not yet been collated with other prints.
source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Khro bo'i bar do 'char tshul bstan pa (the wrathful deities), pages 98–107 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text ga), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: Again, thus face-introduced though, habitual-tendencies bad-by back led, and, terror-fright arisen, then, fled-because, yidam-as face not knowing, and, not meeting there-are-because:
sentences.i: But even when pointed out in this way, some are drawn back by bad habitual tendencies, are struck with terror and fright and flee; and because there are those who do not know them as their yidam and do not recognise,
sentences.n: The part begins on the line where 010 ended, after the eleventh day. ngo sprad kyang, 'though pointed out' (sprad, the past of sprod). bag chags ngan pas, 'by bad habitual tendencies', with -s, 'by'. phyir khrid de, 'is led back, drawn away': khrid is the past stem of 'khrid, 'to lead'; de is the form of ste after -d. dngangs skrag skyes nas, bros pas: the words of the days before. ngo ma shes te ma 'phrod pa yod pas, 'because there are (those) who do not know and do not meet': yod pa, 'there being', with -s, 'because', runs on to the next sentence. The other recension has ngo ma 'phrod pa srid pas, 'because it can happen that they do not recognise'; the print says the same in more words.

sentences.l: Again, day twelfth on, blood-drinking karma family's deity-host and, Gaurīs and, Phra-men and, Sme-ma and, Īśvarīs (plural) welcoming for come, and: face not knowing-ly, terror-fright great-to came-because:
sentences.i: on the twelfth day the host of blood-drinking deities of the karma family, with the Gaurīs, the Phra men, the Sme ma and the Īśvarīs, comes to meet him; and because he does not recognise them, his terror and fright grow great.
sentences.n: zhag bcu gnyis pa, 'the twelfth day' (bcu gnyis, 'ten-two'). las kyi rigs, 'the family of action' (las, 'deed, karma'), the family of Amoghasiddhi, the buddha of the fifth day. Here the goddesses who stand round the five blood-drinkers are named in classes, each with dang, 'and'. go'u ri ma, Sanskrit Gaurī in Tibetan letters with the feminine -ma; below the print also writes ga'u ri. phra men, a Tibetan name for the animal-headed goddesses who follow the Gaurīs; its origin is not explained in the text. dbang phyug ma, 'Lady' (dbang phyug, 'lord', Sanskrit īśvara, with -ma), the Īśvarīs who come last. sme ma is not explained: it may stand for the goddesses of the charnel ground, like Śmaśānī below, or for the four gatekeepers, who are otherwise missing from the list; the other recension has no sme ma and has phra men ma. bsu ba la 'ong, 'come to welcome'. che ru 'ongs pas, 'because (the fear) has come to be great': ru, 'to', after a vowel; 'ongs, the past stem of 'ong, 'to come'. The other recension has ngo mi shes par skrag tu 'ong bas, 'because, not recognising, they come to be afraid'.

sentences.i: This is how he is pointed out. Again call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family,
sentences.n: The formula of the days before, but the print has bod la where it has bos la everywhere else, and again below (101.5): bos is the past stem of 'bod, 'to call'. The da is clear on the image; bod may be the print's spelling of 'bod without its prefix, or of the future bod, so it is kept and read 'call'. The reading is not certain enough to correct. The print has no ma yengs par nyon cig, 'listen without distraction', which the other recension has here. The print runs ming and nas together across the line join and the ornament of the leaf front, here divided.

sentences.n: song ba'i dus su, 'at the time when (twelve days) have gone' (song, the past of 'gro, 'to go'). sentences.l: You-yourself's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid! Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi itself is. Devotion and respect do! Face-knowing and freeing together comes.
sentences.i: He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid. In truth he is the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi himself. Have devotion and respect. Recognising and freedom come together.
sentences.n: Karma Heruka is Amoghasiddhi (Don yod grub pa, 'He Whose Aim Is Accomplished'), the buddha of the fifth day. Here the print has no yab yum, 'with his consort', which it has on the days before and the other recension has here, and closes the sentence with yin no, 'he is', where the days before had yin pas, 'because he is', running on to the command that follows ('so do not fear' on the eighth day, 'so have devotion' on the tenth and eleventh); here mos pa dang gus pa gyis shig stands as a sentence of its own. mos pa dang gus pa, 'devotion and respect' (gus pa, 'respect, reverence'); the other recension adds dung dung, 'intensely, with longing'. mnyam du 'ong ngo, 'come together', where the days before had dus mnyam du, 'at the same time'.

sentences.i: It is like this: a stuffed lion is only what it is, but if one does not see the point, terror and fright arise; and when someone points out to one that this is all it is, one sees through it and is rid of fear. In the same way,
sentences.n: de yang, 'that is to say', opens the explanation of the example. 'di ltar yin gyi, 'it is (only) like this, but': gyi after a verb marks a contrast, 'it is so, but (one does not see it)'. The print closes the phrase with the plain double stroke །། instead of ༔. don ma rtogs na, 'if the meaning is not understood' (rtogs, 'to understand'): ma ... na. skyes te, 'arise, and'. mi gcig gis, 'by one person, by someone'. 'di ltar yin gyi ngo sprad pas, 'because he points out (that) it is like this': gyi is here read as gyis or as marking the words pointed out; the other recension has gyis. mtshang rigs te, 'seeing the hidden thing' (mtshang, 'what is concealed, a flaw'), where the other recension has mtshang rig ste: rigs is the print's spelling of rig, 'to see, to know'. sentences.l: Face-introduction this obtained as-soon-as, self-appearance-or yidam-as face-knowing, then: before earlier-at lama-by instructed's clear-light mother and; later dawned's self-arisen's clear-light, two, mother-child meet, and:
sentences.i: But as soon as one receives this pointing out, one knows them as one's own appearance or as the yidam, and the two meet as mother and child: the clear light the lama taught before, the mother, and the self-arisen clear light that dawns now.
sentences.n: thob ma thag tu, 'as soon as (it) is obtained'. rang snang ngam, 'self-appearance or': -am, 'or', takes the last letter of the word before it (ngam after -ng). sngar gong du, 'before, earlier', two words for one thing. bla is doubtful ([?]): bla mas gdams pa'i, 'that the lama instructed', with bla ma and -s, 'by'; the other recension has sngar goms pa'i, 'that one has grown used to before', in place of gong du bla mas gdams pa'i. 'od gsal ma, 'the mother clear light', the clear light of reality, known in practice; phyis shar ba'i rang byung gi 'od gsal, 'the self-arisen clear light that dawns later', the child, met now in the bardo (shar, the past of 'char; rang byung, 'arising of itself'). ma bu, 'mother and child', as in the parts before. 'phrad de, 'meet, and' ('phrad, 'to meet'); the other recension has 'dres te, 'mingle'.

sentences.i: from the south-west the dark green Ghasmarī, holding in her left hand a skull-cup filled with blood, stirring it with the vajra in her right and drinking it (... ?);
sentences.n: gsma ri is doubtful ([?]): the first stack is read gsma, where the other recension has kasma rī; the name is Ghasmarī. khrag gis bkang ba, 'filled with blood'. g.yas pa'i rdo rjes, 'with the vajra of the right (hand)': rdo rje with -s, 'by'. dkrugs cing, 'stirring, and': dkrugs is the past stem of dkrug, 'to stir, to churn'; the other recension has dkrug. The words after it, nyams pa'i chu la gris, are obscure, and both nyams and chu are doubtful on the image ([?]); the editor looked at them again at four times enlargement and kept the reading with its marks. Word by word they give 'with a knife(?) at the water of the spoiled(?)': nyams pa, 'spoiled, broken'; chu, 'water'; gris, perhaps gri, 'knife', with -s, 'by'. None of this fits the sentence, and the sense of the phrase is uncertain; the idiomatic line leaves it out. The other recension has only dkrug cing zhal du gsol ba, 'stirs it and drinks'. The print uses zhal du gsol ba, 'puts to the mouth', for drinking as for eating.

sentences.l: Lands' Phra-men-women eight-all also blood-drinking fathers five to surrounded, then, own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawned come. Them at not fear! Whatever dawned all, self-appearance, knowing's energy-as face-knowing do!
sentences.i: These eight Phra men of the lands, too, surrounding the five blood-drinking fathers, come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. Do not fear them. Whatever dawns, recognise it all as your own appearance, the energy of awareness.
sentences.n: As for the Gaurīs above. shar 'ong ngo, 'come dawning': the print writes 'ong ngo contracted, as one syllable ('ongo), written out here as on the other pages; shar, the past of 'char, stands where the print elsewhere has 'char du. gang shar thams cad, 'all whatever dawns'. rig pa'i rtsal du, 'as the energy of awareness'; the other recension has rig pa'i ngang du, 'in the state of awareness'.

glossary.གྱིས་ཤིག: gyis shig — do! (gyis, imperative of byed 'do', + shig, which marks a command)
glossary.གྲིས: gris — uncertain: perhaps gri 'knife' + -s 'by', in an obscure phrase (nyams pa'i chu la gris); the sense is not sure
glossary.གྲོལ་བ: grol ba — being freed, liberation (grol + ba, which makes a verb into a noun)
glossary.གྲོལ་ལོ: grol lo — is freed, was freed (grol 'be freed' + the sentence-ending -lo)
glossary.གློ་སྙིང: glo snying — lungs and heart (glo 'lung' + snying 'heart')
glossary.ངན་པས: ngan pas — by the bad (ngan pa 'bad' + -s 'by')
glossary.ངོ: ngo — face; the nature or identity of a thing
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲད: ngo sprad — pointing out, face-introduction (ngo sprad, past of ngo sprod 'point out')
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲད་པ: ngo sprad pa — pointed out, the pointing out (ngo sprad, past of ngo sprod, + pa)
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲད་པས: ngo sprad pas — by being pointed out (ngo sprad 'point out' + -pa + -s 'by')
glossary.ངོ་སྤྲོད: ngo sprod — to point out, to introduce: to bring someone face to face with a thing so that he recognises it (ngo 'face' + sprod 'bring together')
glossary.ཅིང: cing — and, while (links two verbs; also shing, zhing)
glossary.ཆར་བའི: char ba'i — of the dawning, at the dawning (char, the print's spelling of 'char 'dawn', + -ba + -'i 'of'): char ba'i tshe 'at the time of dawning'
glossary.ཆུ: chu — water (chu) · in the obscure phrase nyams pa'i chu la gris, perhaps 'water'; the sense of the phrase is uncertain and chu is doubtful on the image
glossary.ཆུ་སྲིན: chu srin — water monster, the makara (chu 'water' + srin 'monster'), a sea creature like a crocodile
glossary.ཆེ་རུ: che ru — greatly, to be great (che 'great' + -ru 'to'): 'jigs skrag che ru 'ongs 'fear has come to be great'
glossary.ཇམས་པ: jams pa — as printed, uncertain: jams gives no sense; perhaps a cutting error for rngam pa 'fierce', which the other recension has; read 'fierce(?)'
glossary.ཉམས: nyams — decline, wane, be damaged (nyams); of a vow, 'broken' · meditative experience (nyams): nyams kyang read, as a guess, 'even if (he) has experience' (uncertain)
glossary.ཉམས་པའི: nyams pa'i — of the broken, that is spoiled (nyams pa 'to be damaged, to lapse' + -'i 'of'): dam tshig nyams pa'i 'whose commitments are broken' · in the obscure phrase nyams pa'i chu la gris, 'spoiled(?)' is a word-by-word guess (uncertain)
glossary.ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད: nyi shu rtsa brgyad — twenty-eight (nyi shu 'twenty' + rtsa, which joins the units to the tens, + brgyad 'eight')
glossary.ཉོན་ཅིག: nyon cig — listen! (nyon, imperative of nyan 'listen', + cig, which marks a command)
glossary.ཏེ: te — and, and so: links a verb to what follows (te, the form of ste after n, r, l; this print also writes it after other letters)
glossary.ཏྲི་ཤུལ: tri shul — trident (Sanskrit triśūla, in a Tibetan spelling)
glossary.ཐ་མ: tha ma — lowest, last (tha ma): tha ma'i yang tha ma 'the lowest even of the lowest'
glossary.ཐིམ: thim — to dissolve, to be absorbed (thim)
glossary.ཐུགས་པའི: thugs pa'i — uncertain; as printed, with thugs 'mind' (respectful), no sense; read, as a guess, as thug pa'i 'of reaching' (thug 'reach, meet' + -pa'i 'of')
glossary.ཐོགས: thogs — holding, carrying (thogs): thogs nas 'having held'
glossary.དཀར་མོ: dkar mo — white, a white one (dkar 'white' + -mo, feminine)
glossary.དཀར་སེར: dkar ser — whitish yellow, white-yellow (dkar 'white' + ser 'yellow')
glossary.དཀྲུགས: dkrugs — stirred, churned (dkrugs, past stem of dkrug 'to stir, churn')
glossary.དག: dag — pure, correct · plural marker after de: de dag 'those, these' · plural marker after nouns too: sgom chen dag 'great meditators', gzhan dag 'others'
glossary.དང: dang — and; with · after a verb: 'as soon as' (brgyal bsangs pa dang 'as soon as the faint has cleared')
glossary.དངངས་ཤིག: dngangs shig — be terrified! (dngangs + shig, which marks a command); ma dngangs shig 'do not be terrified'
glossary.དངངས་སྐྲག: dngangs skrag — dread and terror (dngangs, the print's spelling of sngangs 'dread', + skrag 'be frightened')
glossary.དཔེར་ན: dper na — for example, as (dpe 'example' + -r 'as' + na 'if')
glossary.དབང་ཕྱུག་མ: dbang phyug ma — Īśvarī, 'Lady' (dbang phyug 'lord', Sanskrit īśvara, + -ma, feminine): the goddesses who come last in the host of the wrathful deities
glossary.དམར་སེར: dmar ser — red-yellow, orange, tawny (dmar 'red' + ser 'yellow')
glossary.དུར་བྱའི: dur bya'i — of the charnel-ground bird (dur 'charnel ground' + bya 'bird' + -'i 'of'): a carrion bird
glossary.དུས་ཚོད: dus tshod — time, moment, occasion (dus 'time' + tshod 'measure')
glossary.དུས་སུ: dus su — at the time (dus + su 'at')
glossary.དེ: de — that; he, it. After a verb (also te, ste): 'and then'
glossary.དེ་ནས: de nas — then, after that (de 'that' + nas 'from')
glossary.དེ་ལྟར: de ltar — thus, in that way (de 'that' + ltar 'like')
glossary.དོན: don — meaning, point, matter; a heading or part of a text
glossary.དོན་ཆེན: don chen — the great matter (don 'matter, aim' + chen 'great')
glossary.དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ: don yod grub pa — Amoghasiddhi, 'He Whose Aim Is Accomplished' (don yod 'not in vain' + grub pa 'accomplished'): the buddha of the north and of the fifth day
glossary.དྲག་པོའི: drag po'i — of the fierce, of the strong (drag po 'fierce' + -'i 'of')
glossary.དྲིལ་བུ: dril bu — bell (dril bu), the hand-bell
glossary.ན: na — if, when (after the verb); also 'in, at' · to be ill, sickness (na, the verb of na ba): skye rga na 'chi 'birth, ageing, sickness and death'
glossary.ནག་མོ: nag mo — black, a black one (nag 'black' + -mo, feminine)
glossary.ནང: nang — inside, within (nang): 'od kyi nang nas 'from within the light'
glossary.ནམ་མཁའི: nam mkha'i — of the sky, of space (nam mkha' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ནས: nas — from; after a verb: 'having done, and then'
glossary.ནི: ni — as for: marks the topic of the sentence
glossary.པདྨ: padma — lotus (Sanskrit padma, written with stacked letters; said 'pema'). Here the Lotus family, the deities grouped around Amitābha · the flower itself, as an emblem held in the hand: phyag na padma bsnams pa 'holding a lotus in the hand'
glossary.པུ་ཀ་སི: pu ka si — Pukkasī (Sanskrit pukkasī, written pu ka si): one of the eight Gaurīs
glossary.ཕག་གདོང: phag gdong — sow-faced, pig-faced (phag 'pig, sow' + gdong 'face')
glossary.ཕྱག: phyag — hand (phyag), the respectful word; also 'homage'
glossary.ཕྱི་རིམ: phyi rim — outer ring, outer tier (phyi 'outer' + rim 'tier, ring')
glossary.ཕྱི་རིམ་དུ: phyi rim du — in the outer tier, on the outer ring (phyi 'outer' + rim 'tier, ring' + -du 'in')
glossary.ཕྱིར: phyir — outside, outward(?). The reading is uncertain; another print has dri med, 'stainless', here · here plainly 'out, outward' (phyi 'outside' + -r): phyir log 'turn back out', phyir thon 'come out' · back: phyir mi ldog go 'does not turn back' (phyir 'back' + ldog 'turn') · because, for the sake of (de'i phyir 'therefore', ci'i phyir 'why'; yod pa'i phyir 'because there is')
glossary.ཕྲ་མེན: phra men — Phra men, a class of animal-headed goddesses who follow the Gaurīs (phra men); the origin of the name is not explained
glossary.ཕྲ་མེན་མ: phra men ma — Phra men, with the feminine ending (phra men + -ma): the animal-headed goddesses
glossary.ཕྲ་མོ: phra mo — thin, fine, subtle (phra mo, phra 'fine' + -mo) · as printed in phra mo dmar mo, uncertain: perhaps the name of a goddess, given as Pramohā; or a slip for phra men, the class of goddesses (the other recension has phra men dmar mo)
glossary.ཕྲག: phrag — shoulder (phrag): phrag la khur nas 'carrying on the shoulder'
glossary.ཕྲལ: phral — torn apart, separated (phral, past stem of 'phral 'to separate, tear apart')
glossary.བཀང: bkang — filled (bkang, past stem of 'gengs 'to fill'): dmar gyi bkang 'filled with red'
glossary.བཀང་བ: bkang ba — filled (bkang, past stem of 'gengs 'to fill' + -ba)
glossary.བཀལ: bkal — perhaps loaded, carried (bkal, past stem of 'gel 'to load'); doubtful on the image, and the sense is not sure
glossary.བག་ཆགས: bag chags — habitual tendencies, the traces past actions leave in the mind (bag chags; Sanskrit vāsanā)
glossary.བགྲད་པ: bgrad pa — spread wide, set apart (bgrad + -pa); said of legs planted in a wide stance
glossary.བཅས་ཏེ: bcas te — together with (bcas + te; dang bcas te: 'along with')
glossary.བཅུ་གཉིས་པ: bcu gnyis pa — twelfth (bcu gnyis 'twelve' + -pa, which makes the ordinal)
glossary.བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས: bcom ldan 'das — the Blessed One, a title of a buddha (bcom ldan 'das, Sanskrit bhagavān; 'das 'gone beyond')
glossary.བཟང་པོ: bzang po — good (bzang po): gang zag bzang po 'a good person'
glossary.བཟུང: bzung — held, seized (bzung, the past stem of 'dzin 'hold': 'dzin / bzung / gzung / zung): bzung yang ma zin pa 'held, yet not caught'
glossary.བར་པ: bar pa — the middle one (bar 'between, middle' + -pa)
glossary.བརྒྱ་བྱིན: brgya byin — Indra (brgya byin, 'Hundred Offerings', the Tibetan name of Indra); also the name of his goddess, Indrāṇī, one of the Īśvarīs
glossary.བརྒྱད་པོ: brgyad po — all eight (brgyad 'eight' + -po, which gathers the whole set)
glossary.བལྟ: blta — to look (blta, future stem of lta 'look'): blta mi bzod pa 'unbearable to look at'
glossary.བལྟ་བ: blta ba — looking, gazing (blta, future stem of lta 'look', + -ba)
glossary.བསིགས་པ: bsigs pa — perhaps shaking, tossing (bsigs + -pa); the sense is not sure
glossary.བསུ་བ: bsu ba — meeting, welcoming, going out to meet someone (bsu 'to meet, welcome' + -ba); bsu ba la 'ongs 'come to meet'
glossary.བསྐོར: bskor — surrounded, encircled (bskor, past of skor 'to surround, to circle')
glossary.བསྒྲགས་པས: bsgrags pas — by proclaiming, because it is proclaimed (bsgrags, past stem of sgrog 'to proclaim, cry aloud' (sgrog / bsgrags / bsgrag / sgrogs) + -pa + -s 'by, because')
glossary.བསྣམས: bsnams — holding, held (bsnams, past stem of snom, the respectful verb 'to take, to hold' (snom / bsnams / bsnam / snoms))
glossary.བསྣོལ: bsnol — crossed, interlaced (bsnol, past stem of snol 'to cross, interlace'): bsnol nas 'having crossed'
glossary.བེ་ཏ་ལི: be ta li — Vetālī (Sanskrit vetālī, written be ta li; be is doubtful on the image, the other recension has be ta lī): one of the eight Gaurīs
glossary.བོད: bod — will call, to call (bod, the future stem of 'bod 'to call') · as printed in bod la, where bos la 'called, and' stands elsewhere in the same formula: perhaps 'bod without its prefix, or the future bod; read 'call' (uncertain)
glossary.བྱ་ཀྲི་མུ་ཁ: bya kri mu kha — Vyāghrīmukhā, 'Tiger-Faced' (Sanskrit vyāghrī 'tigress' + mukhā 'faced', written bya kri mu kha): one of the eight Phra men
glossary.བྱ་བ: bya ba — called; what is to be done (bya, future of byed 'do', + ba). zhes bya ba: 'so called'
glossary.བྲང་ཁར: brang khar — on the chest (brang kha 'chest' + -r 'on')
glossary.བྲལ་བ: bral ba — free of, parted from (bral 'be parted, separated' + -ba): 'jigs pa bral ba 'free of fear'
glossary.བྲོས་པས: bros pas — because it has fled (bros pa, past of 'bros 'run away', + -s)
glossary.བླ་མའི: bla ma'i — of the lama (bla ma + -'i 'of')
glossary.བླ་མས: bla mas — by the lama (bla ma + -s 'by')
glossary.བྷན་དྷ: bhan dha — skull-cup, vessel (Sanskrit bhāṇḍa 'vessel', in Tibetan letters)
glossary.བྷནྡྷ: bhandha — skull-cup, vessel (Sanskrit bhāṇḍa 'vessel', in Tibetan letters, written in one syllable with the letters stacked; also written bhan dha, in two syllables)
glossary.མ: ma — not (before past and imperative verbs) · in a prohibition also before the present stem: ma byed cig 'do not do!' · mother (ma): ma dang bu 'mother and child'
glossary.མ་ཐག་ཏུ: ma thag tu — as soon as, immediately after (ma 'not' + thag 'distance' + -tu: 'with no interval'): after a verb
glossary.མ་བུ: ma bu — mother and child (ma 'mother' + bu 'child'); in this teaching, the clear light of reality ('mother') and the clear light known in practice ('child')
glossary.མ་མོ: ma mo — mother-goddess, a class of fierce goddesses (ma mo, ma 'mother' + -mo; Sanskrit mātṛkā)
glossary.མགོ་ཅན: mgo can — having the head of, -headed (mgo 'head' + can 'having'): wa mgo can 'fox-headed'
glossary.མགོ་བརྙན: mgo brnyan — head-likeness, a head in the shape of an animal's (mgo 'head' + brnyan 'image, likeness')
glossary.མགོ་མ: mgo ma — one with the head of, -headed (mgo 'head' + -ma, feminine): seng mgo ma 'lion-headed one'
glossary.མངོན་སུམ་དུ: mngon sum du — manifestly, before one's eyes (mngon sum 'manifest' + -du)
glossary.མཉམ་དུ: mnyam du — together, along with (mnyam 'equal, same' + -du)
glossary.མཉམ་པར: mnyam par — equally, as much as (mnyam pa 'equal' + -r)
glossary.མཐིང་ན: mthing na — as printed, na doubtful on the image; read as mthing nag 'dark blue' (mthing 'blue'); uncertain
glossary.མཐོང་གཤོལ: mthong gshol — plough: a spelling of thong gshol (mthong written for thong)
glossary.མཐོང་བར: mthong bar — to see, in seeing (mthong 'see' + -ba + -r): mthong bar lta bur 'like seeing'
glossary.མདའ་གཞུ: mda' gzhu — arrow and bow (mda' 'arrow' + gzhu 'bow')
glossary.མཚང: mtshang — what is concealed, a hidden flaw (mtshang): mtshang rig 'to see through it'
glossary.མི: mi — not (before present and future verbs) · person, human being (mi): 'dris pa'i mi 'a person one has known'
glossary.མོས་པ: mos pa — devotion, trust, interest (mos pa)
glossary.ཙཎྜ་ལི: tsaNDa li — Caṇḍālī (Sanskrit caṇḍālī, written tsaN+Da li; the reading is doubtful on the image): one of the eight Gaurīs
glossary.ཙིཏྟ: tsitta — mind (Sanskrit citta, written in Tibetan letters); also used for the heart, the organ
glossary.ཙོའུ་རི་མ: tso'u ri ma — Caurī (Sanskrit caurī, written tso'u ri, + -ma, feminine): one of the eight Gaurīs
glossary.ཚངས་མ: tshangs ma — Brahmāṇī, Brahmā's lady (tshangs pa 'Brahmā' + -ma, feminine)
glossary.ཚུགས་སུ: tshugs su — fixedly (tshugs 'set, planted' + -su): tshugs su blta 'to gaze fixedly'
glossary.ཚེ་འདས: tshe 'das — one whose life has passed, the dead person (tshe 'life' + 'das 'gone beyond')
glossary.ཞག: zhag — day, a day and night (zhag)
glossary.ཞབས: zhabs — foot, leg (zhabs, the respectful word)
glossary.ཞལ་དུ: zhal du — to the mouth, to the face (zhal 'face, mouth', the respectful word, + -du 'to')
glossary.ཞལ་སྦྱོར་དུ: zhal sbyor du — in union (zhal sbyor 'union', father and mother joined, + -du 'in')
glossary.ཞིང: zhing — and, while: links one verb to the next (zhing, the form used after a vowel and after ng, n, m, r, l, '; also cing, shing) · realm, field; a buddha-field (zhing, short for zhing khams): dag pa'i zhing 'pure realm' · a corpse, in these texts (zhing gi dbyug to 'a corpse as a club', zhing chen 'great field', a human corpse); taken from the words, the sense is not wholly sure
glossary.ཞིང་ཆེན: zhing chen — great field: a human corpse (zhing 'field' + chen 'great'; zhing is a word for a corpse in these texts)
glossary.ཞེས: zhes — so, thus: closes a quotation or a name (like inverted commas)
glossary.འཁོར་བར: 'khor bar — in saṃsāra, in the round ('khor ba 'the round, saṃsāra' + -r 'in')
glossary.འཁོར་ལོ: 'khor lo — wheel ('khor lo); the wheel of the teaching
glossary.འགག: 'gag — narrow pass, crucial point, critical moment ('gag); set phrase 'gag la thug pa
glossary.འགེངས་པ: 'gengs pa — filling, drawing (a bow) ('gengs, the present stem of the verb whose past is bkang, + -pa)
glossary.འགྱུར་རོ: 'gyur ro — becomes, will become ('gyur 'to become, to change' + the sentence-ending -ro)
glossary.འཆར་དུ: 'char du — to dawn, to arise ('char 'dawn, arise' + -du 'to'): 'char du 'ong 'will dawn'
glossary.འཇིགས་ཤིག: 'jigs shig — be afraid! ('jigs 'fear' + shig, which marks a command); ma 'jigs shig 'do not be afraid'
glossary.འདི་ལྟར: 'di ltar — in this way, like this ('di 'this' + ltar 'like')
glossary.འདི་སྐད་དོ: 'di skad do — these words (are said) ('di 'this' + skad 'speech' + the sentence-ending -do)
glossary.འདིར: 'dir — here, in this ('di + -r 'in') · in 'dir btsam du, as printed, perhaps for ldir 'roaring' (ldir ba tsam du 'as loud as the roaring of'); a guess
glossary.འདྲ་བར: 'dra bar — like, in the same way ('dra ba 'alike' + -r)
glossary.འདྲིས: 'dris — familiar, familiarity ('dris): sngar 'dris med pa 'without earlier familiarity'
glossary.འཕྲད: 'phrad — to meet, to come upon ('phrad): X dang 'phrad 'to meet with X'
glossary.འཕྲད་བ: 'phrad ba — meeting ('phrad, 'to meet', + -ba; the print's spelling of 'phrad pa): 'phrad ba ltar 'like meeting'
glossary.འཕྲོད་པ: 'phrod pa — meeting, recognition ('phrod 'to meet' + -pa): ngo 'phrod pa 'the recognition'
glossary.འཛིན་པ: 'dzin pa — grasping, holding ('dzin 'hold' + -pa): the mind taking hold of what it sees · holding with compassion (thugs rjes 'dzin pa)
glossary.འོང: 'ong — comes, happens, it may happen that ('ong 'come')
glossary.འོངས་པས: 'ongs pas — having come, therefore ('ongs, past of 'ong 'come', + -pas 'because')
glossary.འོད་གསལ: 'od gsal — clear light, luminosity: the nature of mind, said to show itself bare at death ('od 'light' + gsal 'clear')
glossary.ཡང: yang — also, even, though (written kyang after g, d, b, s) · again, once more, at the head of a sentence (yang ngo sprad pa ni 'and the pointing out again')
glossary.ཡབ: yab — father (yab, respectful); the male of a buddha and his consort
glossary.ཡབ་ཡུམ: yab yum — father and mother; a buddha and his consort in union (yab 'father' + yum 'mother')
glossary.ཡི་དམ: yi dam — yidam, one's chosen deity (yi dam)
glossary.ཡི་དམ་དུ: yi dam du — as the yidam (yi dam 'one's chosen deity' + -du 'as, to')
glossary.ཡིན་ནོ: yin no — is, are (yin 'to be' + the sentence-ending -no)
glossary.ཡུམ: yum — mother; a buddha's female partner, consort (yum)
glossary.ཡེངས་པར: yengs par — distractedly, in distraction (yengs pa 'to be distracted' + -r): ma yengs par 'undistracted'
glossary.ཡོད་པས: yod pas — because there is (yod 'there is' + -pas 'because')
glossary.རང་གསལ་དུ: rang gsal du — as clear of itself, self-clear (rang 'self' + gsal 'clear' + -du 'as, to')
glossary.རང་གྲོལ་དུ: rang grol du — as freed of itself, of itself freed (rang grol 'freed of itself' + -du 'as, to')

about: The third part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities: day twelve and the first of the wrathful goddesses. Those who, for all the pointing out, are drawn back by bad habits and flee in terror meet, on the twelfth day, the blood-drinkers of the karma family with the Gaurīs, the Phra men and the Īśvarīs. Karma Heruka, dark green, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, holding a sword, a khaṭvāṅga, a staff, a bell, a skull-cup and a plough, embraced by his consort Karmakrodhīśvarī, dawns from the north of the dead person's own brain. He is not to be feared: he is the dead person's own yidam, and in truth Amoghasiddhi, and to recognise him is to be freed. The text explains why this works: as a man who is told that a lion is only a stuffed one loses his fear, so one who has the lama's instruction knows the huge blood-drinkers for his own appearance, and the clear light taught before and the clear light that dawns now meet like mother and child. Then come, each from a quarter of the brain and each with her colour and what she holds, the eight Gaurīs of the sacred places, the eight Phra men of the lands with the heads of lion, tiger, fox, wolf, vulture, charnel bird, crow and owl, the four gatekeepers with the heads of tiger, sow, lion and snake, and, in the outer ring of the thirty deities of the fierce heruka, the twenty-eight Īśvarīs with their many heads and weapons, of whom the six yoginīs of the east are described here. Again and again the dead person is told not to fear them and to recognise whatever dawns as his own appearance, the energy of awareness.
